The lunchtime fixing
Notice 304/26, struck 12:23 UK: standard maturity 2-year 5.23% (−1bp vs this morning), 5-year 5.50% (−1bp), 10-year 5.98% (−2bp), 20-year 6.53% (−1bp), 50-year 6.41% (−1bp); annuity and EIP profiles eased 1–2bp the same way (full table above). In plain terms: borrowing at lunchtime cost slightly less than at this morning's round, giving back a small part of the morning's 4–6bp rise.
US jobs miss — and what it means for Monday's rate
The US economy lost 23,000 jobs in July against expectations of an 80,000 gain, and June's figure was revised down to +20,000; the unemployment rate ticked down to 4.1%. A shrinking US payroll is a genuine surprise, and rates markets moved promptly: the one-year SONIA swap — a gauge of what markets expect the Bank of England to do over the next year — fell to 4.05%, down 4.6bp on the day, most of it after 13:30. Our estimate of the next PWLB fixing (Monday ~09:15, since today's rounds are done) is now below today's lunchtime levels: 5-year 5.46% vs 5.50% fixed, 10-year 5.95% vs 5.98%, 20-year 6.50% vs 6.53%. Treasurer's read: if this afternoon's rally holds into Monday morning, Monday's rates should price a few basis points below today's — a borrower with discretion on timing may prefer Monday's morning round to locking this afternoon's levels. That is labelled judgement about direction, not a promise; the weekend's news flow can move it either way.
Rest of day
The end-of-day summary lands as usual around 17:30 UK with the full day's picture. Beyond that, the UK calendar is quiet until Thursday's preliminary Q2 GDP figures (07:00 UK, 13 August). What markets expect from the Bank of England is unchanged in shape today — no change priced for September's meeting, with the next move still expected around November.

That was wrong: PWLB rates are set around 09:00–09:15 and 12:25–12:30 UK, so a 13:30 release lands after the day's final fixing. Payrolls will move markets this afternoon — and that shapes Monday morning's fixing, not today's. Thanks to our reader for the catch; the timetable is now a hard rule in the operating manual.
Midday state of play: rates have eased back from this morning's fixing — our estimate of the next PWLB rate sits 1.1–1.7bp below the 09:06 fix on every tenor. The PM fixing strikes around 12:25–12:30; US payrolls at 13:30 lands after it and shapes Monday's fixing instead.
Where we stand at midday
Since the 09:06 fixing (10y at 6.00%), gilt-driven pricing has drifted a touch lower: our next-fix estimates now sit at 5y 5.495%, 10y 5.983%, 20y 6.528% — all 1.1–1.7bp below this morning's fixed rates (the chart above shows each tenor). Short-term rate expectations have eased in parallel: 1y OIS at 4.085%, down 1.1bp on the day. In plain terms: if the PM fixing struck on current levels, borrowing would cost a shade over a basis point less than it did this morning — drift, not a move.
The afternoon, in order
~12:25–12:30 — the PM fixing strikes on whatever the gilt market is doing at that moment; we cover it as soon as the notice reaches the API. 13:30 — US payrolls (forecast 80K jobs added vs 57K last month; unemployment expected steady at 4.2%): the week's biggest global data point. A strong number would push borrowing costs up into next week; a weak one would pull them down — either way the effect lands in Monday's AM fixing, and our event pass at 13:40 will report the print and the market's first reaction.

i Timing note. Gilts open at 08:00 and the prediction engine re-anchors then — the implieds above are the overnight carry from the 17:59 close, not a live read. Borrower badges resume once the guard clears at the open.
AM fixing lands ~09:15 with the engine carrying +2.3–3.4bp from last night's close. Overnight: China's export beat, a new US 15% tariff on a key chip material, and talk of a Hormuz de-escalation deal. The day's main event is US payrolls at 13:30 UK.
Overnight
China's July trade data beat: exports +23.9% YoY (f'cast 22.2%), surplus $112.5B (f'cast $107.0B), imports a touch soft at 27.5%. At 02:03 UK, reports that the US is imposing a 15% tariff on a key chip material to counter China — an escalation with an inflationary edge. Pointing the other way, overnight Iran-war coverage has Trump saying the war “can't go much longer” with a Hormuz deal reportedly close — de-escalation there would ease the oil channel that has been pressuring gilts all year. Also on the watch list: Taiwan's president was evacuated during the night (developing, no market fingerprint yet). At home, Lloyds house prices came in flat — 0% MoM, 0.1% YoY vs 0.4% forecast — another cooling-housing print; the euro-area trade surplus missed at €15.4B.
Today
The AM fixing is due ~09:15 UK. If the overnight carry holds, the engine implies standard maturity at 5y 5.491% (+3.1bp), 10y 5.968% (+2.8), 20y 6.523% (+2.3), 50y 6.406% (+2.6) vs yesterday's PM fix. Then US Non-Farm Payrolls at 13:30 UK (f'cast 80K vs 57K prior; unemployment f'cast steady at 4.2%) — the week's biggest global print and a direct input to the front end ahead of the PM fixing round. Minor: BBA mortgage rate at 10:00.
Ahead
The OIS-implied Bank Rate path is unchanged into the morning: 17 Sep on hold at 3.75%, next +25bp priced for Nov 2026, 4.25% by Mar 2027. UK calendar stays quiet until the preliminary Q2 GDP set next Thursday, 13 Aug 07:00 UK (QoQ f'cast 0.2%, YoY prel 1.6%).

The day in rates
Benchmark gilts closed higher across the curve vs Wednesday: ~2y 0.5% Jan29 4.259% (+5.8bp), ~5y 1% Jan32 4.546% (+4.6), ~10y 1.75% Sep37 5.102% (+4.4), ~30y 1.75% Jul57 5.673% (+3.9), longest 1.125% Oct73 5.244% (+4.2). Money markets moved with them: intraday 1y OIS 4.096% vs 4.053% previous close (+4.3bp); the 6M SONIA forward +2.6bp. No domestic releases this afternoon (the 09:30 Construction PMI beat was covered in the morning passes) and no rates-relevant headlines in the monitored feeds; one broader news sweep found no dated catalyst for the move — a broad, front-led repricing with no obvious single trigger, so none is asserted.
PM fixing 302/26 — flat on the morning
The 12:25 fixing moved at most 1bp against the AM round (standard 2y +1bp, 10y −1bp; every other published segment unchanged) — all three profiles in the table above. Borrower read: today's certainty came at 5.46% (5y), 5.94% (10y), 6.50% (20y) standard maturity — unchanged from the morning, so nothing was given up by transacting PM.
Tomorrow and ahead
If tonight's close holds, the engine implies the next standard-maturity fixes at 5y 5.491% (+3.1bp), 10y 5.968% (+2.8), 20y 6.523% (+2.3), 50y 6.406% (+2.6). Engine guard is closed (after-hours), so borrower badges are withheld until the morning re-anchor — full engine output in the appendix. The OIS-implied Bank Rate path still has 17 Sep on hold at 3.75%, the next +25bp priced for Nov 2026 (to 4.00%), and 4.25% by Mar 2027. UK calendar is quiet until the preliminary Q2 GDP set next Thursday, 13 Aug 07:00 UK (QoQ f'cast 0.2%, YoY prel 1.6% vs 0.9% prior, MoM 0.1%).
